display_name: Lafage, Côtes Catalanes Vieilles Vignes Tessellae
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Old vines over 100 years old on black schist soils drive the concentration in this Côtes Catalanes red. Lafage sources Tessellae from low-yielding bush vines near Perpignan, yielding dark Syrah fruit laced with Carignan's iron and garrigue. At $15, it punches above generic Languedoc blends.",
  "wine_summary": "Lafage crafts Tessellae from centenarian vines across Roussillon's schist-dominated foothills, blending Syrah, Carignan, Grenache, and Mourvèdre for a field blend snapshot of the site's rugged potential. Jean-Marc Lafage farms organically here, prioritizing bush-trained old vines that survive on minimal water, which concentrates flavors into blackberry, olive tapenade, and volcanic smoke—far from the flabby overcropped reds that plague entry-level IGP wines. This 14.5% ABV bottling earned silver from Berliner Wine Trophy for vintages like 2012, proving Roussillon's value in a sea of pricier Rhône wannabes.",
  "terroir_expression": "Black schist and gneiss soils in the Pyrénées-Orientales department fracture easily, forcing vine roots deep for water and minerals that translate to graphite-edged tannins and blood-iron notes from Carignan, while the Mediterranean climate—hot days cooled by Tramontane winds off the Pyrenees—preserves Syrah's black pepper snap and Grenache's baked plum density. Vieilles Vignes status means yields under 20 hl/ha, amplifying Mourvèdre's gamey meatiness into a chewy, site-specific core that dusty hillside sites deliver without irrigation.",
  "vinification_summary": "Lafage destems and ferments in concrete tanks with indigenous yeasts to retain fruit purity, followed by short macerations that soften Carignan's rustic tannins without oak dominance. Partial carbonic maceration on Grenache parcels extracts brighter red fruit and rounds edges, a technique borrowed from Beaujolais that counters the blend's natural density from 14.5% alcohol. No fining or filtration preserves the old-vine grit.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken thrives with the wine's iron tannins cutting spice and schist-driven smoke echoing cayenne heat. Lamb tagine matches Mourvèdre's game notes against preserved lemon and cumin for textural lift. Braised short ribs pull Syrah's dark fruit into umami synergy on fine dining plates. Chorizo paella pairs casually as Carignan's herbs amplify saffron and rice earthiness. Grilled octopus skewers work seaside because peppery Syrah slices charred tentacles.",
  "comparable_wines": "Domaine de la Janasse Côtes du Rhône — shares Syrah-Carignan drive but with more clay softness versus Tessellae's schist bite. Mas Amiel Maury — old-vine Grenache depth akin to Tessellae, though sweeter from appellation rules. Chapoutier Thorngrove Syrah — iron tannins mirror Carignan here, at similar price.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-full red blend with grippy tannins and smoky schist minerality",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2024-2030 for optimal integration of fruit and structure. Store cool and humid to let tannins mellow.",
  "value_assessment": "$14-16 retail positions it against basic Côtes du Rhône like Guigal. Beats overoaked Languedoc competitors like Château de Saint Martin by delivering old-vine focus without fluff. Buy multiples—silver medals confirm reliability.",
  "market_position": "Bistro somms list Tessellae for value-driven Catalan nights alongside tapas. Retail shoppers grab it from LCBO shelves seeking Rhône alternatives under $20. Casual red drinkers favor its approachability over collector Cabernets.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you hate rustic edges—Carignan's iron demands food, unlike polished Priorats. Old-vine blends like this expose why Roussillon beats bloated GSMs from hotter sites. Stock up before prices climb with Lafage's rising profile.",
